(3.14).

Let $\mathcal{X}$ be the universal deformation (Section 2.1) and $\mathcal{A}$ be the global sections of its quantization. Assume that there is a Frobenius-constant quantization (3.13) $\Lambda:\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{X})^{(1)}\to Z(\mathcal{A})$. Then $\Lambda(a)$ for $a\in\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{X})_{0}$, a $T$ -weight zero element (see Section 2.1), acts on the $D$ -module of twisted traces as a central endomorphism.

On the quantum $D$ -module side, quantum Steenrod operations [Fuk97, Wil20] and their equivariant generalizations [Lee25, Lee23] are deformations of the classical Steenrod operations on cohomology with $\mathbb{F}_{p}$ -coefficients, in the same way the quantum cohomology is a deformation of the cohomology ring with the cup product. They arise from suitable $\mathbb{Z}/p$ -equivariant counts of genus $0$ stable maps. It is proven in [SW22, Lee25] that the quantum Steenrod operations are covariantly constant with respect to the quantum connection and commute with each other, thereby giving rise to central endomorphisms of quantum $D$ -modules (3.12):
card.label: Proposition 1.1

paper.title: 3D mirror symmetry in positive characteristic
paper.abstract: Via the formulation of (quantum) Hikita conjecture with coefficients in a characteristic $p$ field, we explain an arithmetic aspect of the theory of 3D mirror symmetry. Namely, we propose that the action of Steenrod-type operations and Frobenius-constant quantizations intertwine under the (quantum) Hikita isomorphism for 3D mirror pairs, and verify this for the Springer resolutions and hypertoric varieties.
